01

Setting specification

Task

Minimize $f$ globally over $B_2(0,R)$ and return a point with small objective gap.

Admissible model

$f$ is convex and continuously differentiable on an open neighborhood of $B_2(0,R+\tau)$, with $\tau>0$. For every $x,y$ in this neighborhood, $\|\nabla f(x)-\nabla f(y)\|_2\le H_\nu\|x-y\|_2^\nu$, where $0<\nu<1$.

Minimize over $B_2(0,R)$, allowing boundary optima. The neighborhood thickness is part of the query permission; a function defined in the ball is not automatically extended to the ambient space.

Oracle interface

At any finite query point $x$ in $B_2(0,R+\tau)$, the oracle returns the single exact scalar $f(x)$. The reply is uniquely determined and contains no gradient, subgradient or derivative-vector product.

Projection and the stated proximal operations over known geometry are free.

The public inputs are $d$, $\nu$, $H_\nu$, $R$, $\tau$, $\varepsilon$, together with the sets, kernels and auxiliary operations explicitly declared above. Information about the unknown objective and any undisclosed sample distribution is obtained only through the stated interface.

Output

Return $\widehat{x}\in B_2(0,R)$. The output may be an unqueried point, an average or convex combination that remains in the stated space. No function value, gradient, inner solution, or accuracy certificate must accompany the output.

Loss or accuracy criterion

The base loss is $\ell(I,x)=f(x)-f_*$, where $f_*=\inf_{u\in B_2(0,R)}f(u)$. This nonnegative loss is evaluated at the output, with tolerance $\varepsilon$.

Resource accounting

Each scalar function value or noisy observation costs $1$ call. Every location in a multipoint finite difference, every initialization query, and every reference observation is charged.

Only the declared oracle resource is charged. Computation and storage using existing information, together with explicitly known geometric and proximal operations, are free.

Algorithm views and success guarantees

Deterministic

Only deterministic strategies are allowed. Queries, stopping and postprocessing may be arbitrary measurable adaptive functions of the history. No linear-span or zero-respecting restriction is imposed.

Interactions are sequential, and every actual response in a batch is charged separately. Except for explicitly listed auxiliary interfaces, arithmetic, linear algebra, storage, and internal computation on available information are free, with no additional communication or memory restriction. Finite-difference steps must be finite and positive; real-number precision is not charged separately.

After fixing the public inputs, choose one algorithm that works for every admissible instance and reply law. The requirement $\ell(I,\widehat{x})\le \varepsilon$ holds deterministically for each instance.

Oracle cost uses a deterministic worst-case budget: $N\le T$ on every possible execution path. For multiple resources, coordinatewise caps apply jointly along the same path.

Randomized

Private randomization is allowed, with the seed independent of the instance and external randomness. Queries, stopping and postprocessing may be arbitrary measurable adaptive functions of the history. No linear-span or zero-respecting restriction is imposed.

Interactions are sequential, and every actual response in a batch is charged separately. Except for explicitly listed auxiliary interfaces, arithmetic, linear algebra, storage, and internal computation on available information are free, with no additional communication or memory restriction. Finite-difference steps must be finite and positive; real-number precision is not charged separately.

After fixing the public inputs, choose one algorithm that works for every admissible instance and reply law. The error requirement is $\Pr(\ell(I,\widehat{x})\le \varepsilon)\ge2/3$.

Probability is over the algorithm's random seed only.

Oracle cost uses a deterministic worst-case budget: $N\le T$ on every possible execution path. For multiple resources, coordinatewise caps apply jointly along the same path.

Output qualification. Random selection among previously queried points is permitted, subject to the declared success guarantee.

/proofs/0/body · SHA-256 00ba7b58f36c9acf20dbb9e3a7e5a040a85cc433dbfe67cc927a54201faaf59f
Writing $W=H_\nu R^{1+\nu}/\varepsilon$, an upper is $O_\nu(d[1+W^{2/(1+3\nu)}])$. A lower $\Omega_\nu(W^{2/(1+3\nu)})$ holds for $W\ge W_{0,\nu}$ and $$d\ge\max\{8,C_\nu W^{8/(1+3\nu)}\log(eW)\}.$$ At any feasible point, forward differences with $0<h\le\tau$ satisfy $\|\widehat g-\nabla f(x)\|\le\sqrt dH_\nu h^\nu/(1+\nu)$. Thus $d+1$ exact values achieve any prescribed positive gradient error. On a set of diameter $2R$, shifting the reported function value downward by $2R\eta$ gives a valid lower first-order model. The upper model error is at most $4R\eta+H_\nu\|y-x\|^{1+\nu}/(1+\nu)$. Young's inequality bounds the latter by $M_\delta\|y-x\|^2/2+\delta/2$, where $M_\delta=C_\nu H_\nu^{2/(1+\nu)}\delta^{-(1-\nu)/(1+\nu)}$. Choose $\eta\le\delta/(8R)$. The universal inexact accelerated model bound is $O(M_\delta R^2/N^2+N\delta)$. Taking $\delta$ a small multiple of $\varepsilon/N$ and solving yields the stated iteration count, multiplied by $O(d)$ values. The additive one is needed because unrestricted affine terms remain legal even if $H_\nu$ is tiny. For the lower use Diakonikolas and Guzman, Theorem 12, at norm $p=2$ and parallel batch size one. Its two terms scale as $W^{2/(1+3\nu)}$ and $dW^{-6/(1+3\nu)}/\log M$. Choose $M$ a small constant multiple of the first term. The displayed dimension makes the second no smaller than the first. The radial shielding in the source construction handles exterior queries, and its ball-contained witness preserves the constrained optimum comparison. If the target returns an unqueried feasible point, append one query there to meet the source's successful-query convention; the $W\ge W_{0,\nu}$ condition absorbs that one call. Scale coordinates by $R$ and values by $H_\nu R^{1+\nu}$. The source lower concerns a stronger local first-order oracle and so also limits exact-value algorithms, without acquiring an extra factor of $d$.

/proofs/1/body · SHA-256 bf1bf3d88d54a714150ea6316d162fbf02e6ffd3a83bffdcd8b8885e7457215e
Retained premises, not historical recertification: /common_specification @ cb48cb4b4baea9df2c2680eec34eefd13baf4283f8883190d24fe490f128f366 supplies the Euclidean feasible/output ball of radius R, scalar exact-value oracle, fixed-path query cost, and the gradient seminorm inequality <=H_nu on the query neighborhood. /views @ 2f0a5ec56525ede164a1e741b632b782e6e1d6a60694e8420371420f75b33245 supplies arbitrary measurable adaptive deterministic algorithms and private-random algorithms with per-instance success >=2/3. /resource_projections/0 @ 51e8191c0794f51712b73e70c0665ecc79d2490f05e1d9dd0bc91c93dd6879de fixes one value per call. The q1 minimax quantities are /quantities/0 @ 8f04168525f60569d0129c9d52a55c82fcf0e8406645a6e3ddf554667b400cea and /quantities/2 @ 98a48d9e22187046a9e92061ea4f10395029a666bb1545cf6c39f1085961c6f5. No external theorem is used below. I. Subclass and preservation. Every f(x)=a.x+b, with arbitrary a in R^d and b in R, is globally convex C1 and has gradient Holder seminorm zero, hence belongs for every permitted positive H_nu and every tau>0. Its constrained minimum is b-R||a||. Each permitted value is the single scalar a.q+b; neither an unqueried output nor free postprocessing yields an additional observation. The subclass retains the original query domain, output ball, guarantees and fixed path caps; it does not impose an affine promise on the target. II. Exact deterministic lower. Suppose a deterministic algorithm has cap k<=d and run it on the admissible zero function. Let q_1,...,q_m, m<=k, be its actual queries and y its feasible output. If m>=1 the m homogeneous equations a.q_i+b=0 in d+1 unknowns admit a nonzero solution (a,b), necessarily with a!=0 because a=0 would force b=0. Choose sign sigma with sigma a.y>=0 and lambda>epsilon/(R||a||). The fixed instance f(x)=sigma lambda(a.x+b) reproduces every response and therefore the entire adaptive transcript and output. Its gap is lambda(sigma a.y+R||a||)>epsilon, a contradiction. If m=0 choose any nonzero a, choose its sign similarly, and scale; no response constraints are needed. Thus T_det>=d+1 exactly, including d=1. III. Exact randomized lower. Let an algorithm have integer cap k. If k>=d, k>=d/9 is immediate; assume k<d. For each L>0 choose a uniformly on the radius-L sphere, independently of its private random tape, and consider f_a(x)=a.x. Fix the tape. Construct an augmented transcript with one new orthogonal linear measurement at each of k steps. Maintain the span of previous augmented directions. If the algorithm's next actual query q has a nonzero orthogonal component, measure along that component's unit direction and reconstruct a.q from that answer and the already measured projection. If q lies in the span its answer is already determined, so measure any measurably selected orthogonal unit direction instead. After the algorithm stops, pad to k steps in the same way. Each such unit-direction measurement can be obtained at (R+tau) times the direction and divided by R+tau, using one permitted scalar value. Only the reconstructed original answers are shown to the original algorithm. Its output Y is therefore measurable in the enlarged history. This construction also handles dependent queries and data-dependent stopping. Conditional on the enlarged history after j measurements and the fixed tape, write a=p_j+z_j. Rotational symmetry shows inductively that z_j is uniform on the sphere of radius sqrt(L^2-||p_j||^2) in the (d-j)-dimensional orthogonal complement: a new predictable orthogonal direction fixes exactly its one coordinate and leaves a uniform orthogonal residual. Consequently E[a|history]=p_j and the next squared-coordinate conditional mean is (L^2-||p_j||^2)/(d-j). Starting at p_0=0, the recursion gives E||p_j||^2=jL^2/d. This proves the needed adaptive measurement statement directly, without an external information theorem. Average also over the private tape. The gap Z=RL+a.Y lies in [0,2RL] and E Z=RL+E[p_k.Y]>=RL-R E||p_k||>=RL(1-sqrt(k/d)). Uniform per-instance success >=2/3, integrated over the sphere, gives Pr(Z<=epsilon)>=2/3. For 2RL>epsilon this implies E Z<=2epsilon/3+2RL/3. Hence sqrt(k/d)>=1/3-2epsilon/(3RL). The fixed algorithm must satisfy this for every L, since slopes have no magnitude bound. Letting L tend to infinity gives k>=d/9 and therefore T_rand>=ceil(d/9) exactly. The constructed instances are fixed before the random tape, so the adversarial-instance quantifier is preserved. IV. Envelope and endpoints. Retain b3/b4 only on their existing contracts and guards: /bounds @ d65950486a96732b19558449b3ee25c31c49fc99c9517c50c71e028cf1aff836, /comparisons @ 6a65a84e8fa068c8ece09c60f2732e04941a530a00704f718a33a858fc633ab6, and ZO_PROOF_HOLDER /proofs/0 @ 8e9b2cccbdd9204cd27a869418c0a80b7c7d0eace21574f0af7378874d978538. Combining either dimension lower with its view's b4 gives Omega_nu(max{d,W^(2/(1+3nu))}) on the existing high-dimensional guard. The upper remains O_nu(d W^(2/(1+3nu))) there; the additive one in b3 is absorbed because W>=W_{0,nu}>0 with nu fixed. Taking their ratio gives O_nu(min{d,W^(2/(1+3nu))}). For W>=1 the dimension condition implies W^(2/(1+3nu))<=C_nu^(-1/4)d^(1/4); for W<1 it is <=1<=d. Thus on the guarded family the new lower is equivalently Omega_nu(d), without asserting an exact crossover constant. Improvement of order occurs when d/W^(2/(1+3nu)) tends to infinity. Both new exact lower bounds are valid on the whole target, so zero calls are impossible at any finite epsilon. The globally valid retained b3 upper and these lowers imply Theta_nu(d) when 0<W<=1, with constants uniform in d,H_nu,R,tau,epsilon. This is a coarse-accuracy consequence, not an extension of b4's source guard or a saturation theorem for fine accuracy. V. Parameter roles. /parameters @ e1be3d294321ee3bab25a05b2d4b9fb30b42ec381b201529b93df389c92e4819 defines W and its dependencies. Under x=Ru and f divided by H_nu R^(1+nu), the Holder budget becomes one and the accuracy becomes 1/W; exact values are rescaled without changing the number of scalar observations. The buffer remains positive, and the retained finite-difference proof uses h<=tau with arbitrary positive h, so its call rate is uniform in tau. ZO_PROOF_HOLDER explicitly fixes 0<nu<1 and uses constants depending on nu. Moving only nu from tracked_parameters to fixed_parameters in the two active q1 records records that existing convention for every fixed nu; it does not restrict the nu domain, change a quantity expression or guarantee, or claim uniformity as nu approaches 0 or 1. The historical q2 identities are not identified with q1.
